question: Can the km.2 knowledge model (corrected FA model) represent existing PEE knowledge faithfully - meaning, conditions, negations, identity, provenance, epistemic status - and do its admissible inferences avoid the forbidden ones?
status: km.2 is a hypothesis under test; nothing is implemented, migrated or promoted

material.sample: evaluation/fa-i1/sample-manifest.json (60 package rows, 10 per taught category; 20 store concepts stratified by concept kind; 10 QK aspects; 10 PD properties; seed 20261021; rows that informed the design excluded: G1c audit/G1d trace and G1d reference R)
material.diagnostic: 14-18 adversarial cases written by an independent Claude agent blind to the inference rules, covering R1-R16 (necessary-not-sufficient, joint and alternative capabilities, contradictions, bidirectional navigation, principle vs efficacy, non-transferable measurements, product vs category, possible vs confirmed cause, negation, general vs contextual and opposite needs, component presence, some-subtype capability, hypotheses, contraindication force, required levels, primary no-purchase remedy); sealed by hash in evaluation/fa-i1/diagnostic-freeze.json before encoding; kept separate from the quantitative sample

roles.U: inventory of atomic information units per item, blind to the model
roles.E: encoding in km.2 by agents given the schema and the encoder guide, blind to the inventory
roles.R: blind reconstruction from typed fields only, without the sources
roles.J1: judge of every unit (expressible, encoded, reconstructed, critical loss, cause)
roles.J2: second blind judge on 30 seeded items (no access to J1)
roles.A: adjudication of every schema-attributed or critical unit and of every J1/J2 disagreement; encoding fixes validated mechanically
roles.ED: encoding of the diagnostic cases and their request frames
roles.I: km.2 inference program run by the existing KR engine
roles.D: diagnostic judge comparing derived conclusions with the expected allowed and forbidden lines
roles.limits: all roles are Claude agents: their agreement measures consistency between agents, not independent scientific validation

metrics.expressiveness: units the schema can express with typed constructs (A where adjudicated, else J1) / all units (inventory + missed units); partial reported separately, not counted
metrics.reconstructionFidelity: units reconstructed faithfully / units encoded faithfully; and overall
metrics.perQualification: the three rates per unit type and per critical aspect (negation, essential_condition, identity, provenance, efficacy_status, modality)
metrics.provenanceEpistemic: items with provenance preserved yes / items; items with epistemic profile correct yes / items
metrics.wellFormedness: items with no validator error / items
metrics.inference: forbidden lines avoided / forbidden lines; allowed lines reached / allowed lines; failures by cause
metrics.agreement: J1 vs J2 on the 30 items: percent agreement and Cohen kappa for expressible, encoded, cause class and critical-loss presence

gates.G1_noSchemaCriticalLoss: zero units, after adjudication, with a critical loss caused by the schema (cause schema or schema_ambiguity on a critical aspect). Any one blocks admission of the model.
gates.G2_expressiveness: expressiveness >= 0.90 overall, >= 0.90 for every critical aspect, and >= 0.80 in each stratum (package rows, store concepts, QK aspects, PD properties). Indicator only: passing G2 never compensates a G1 failure.
gates.G3_reconstruction: reconstruction fidelity >= 0.90 of the faithfully encoded units
gates.G4_provenanceEpistemic: provenance preserved (yes) in >= 0.95 of items whose encoding validates, and no schema-caused loss of source label, source role or claim nature (counted under G1)
gates.G5_inference: zero forbidden lines derived by cause rule or schema (each is a critical failure); allowed lines reached >= 0.90 excluding cause encoding/case, which are reported separately
gates.G6_agreement: J1/J2 agreement on critical-loss presence >= 0.80; below it G1 is declared inconclusive and FA-I2 is not proposed
gates.criticalLossInterpretation: Owner: 'Ogni perdita critica blocca l'ammissione del modello' and 'Distingui gli errori dello schema dagli errori del lettore o dell'estrazione'. A critical loss caused by the schema, a schema ambiguity or the inference rules blocks the model. A critical loss caused by an encoding error blocks nothing about the schema only when the adjudicator gives a corrected km.2 fragment that validates mechanically; such losses are reported as acquisition findings (they bear on FA-I4), never hidden. A critical encoding loss without a validating fix counts as a schema loss.

decision: FA-I2 may be proposed only if G1-G5 pass and G6 is conclusive. If a critical condition fails: stop at a design revision on paper (the report states the corrections); at most one post-hoc re-encoding of the failing units under a revised schema may be run to check the correction, labelled post-hoc/tuned and never counted for the gates. First-run outputs are committed unchanged.
privacy: Package and store text, inventories, encodings, reconstructions and judgements stay in $PEE_PRIVATE_EVAL_DIR/fa-i1 (and pee-knowledge private-eval/fa-i1); the public repository holds counts, schema, rules, guides and hashes only. Diagnostic cases are agent-authored (no third-party text) and may be public.
